title: R2T4 Calculation Dispute Across Merged Campus Records
scenario_text:
**Banner SIS — Student Record (ID: W00298471)**
Name: Daniel Park-Simmons | Campus: East Campus (merged from former 'Eastview Community College' 5 years ago)
Enrollment Spring 2026: 12 credits (full-time) | Withdrawal date: Mar 14, 2026 (official)
Prior ID (legacy Eastview system): EV-10923 | Records migration note: 'Attendance data pre-merge incomplete; LMS is authoritative for post-merge terms'

**Banner Financial Aid — Disbursement Record**
Pell Grant: $3,298 disbursed (Feb 1, 2026) | Institutional Grant: $2,000 disbursed (Feb 1, 2026)
Direct Sub Loan: $1,750 disbursed (Feb 1, 2026) | Total Title IV disbursed: $5,048
R2T4 calculation initiated: Mar 18, 2026 | Status: PENDING — 'Attendance verification required'

**Canvas LMS — Activity Log (Spring 2026, exported Mar 15)**
Daniel Park-Simmons | Course: PSYCH 301 — Last login: Mar 12 | Submissions: 3 of 5 due
Course: ENG 204 — Last login: Mar 14 | Submissions: 4 of 4 due
Course: MATH 210 — Last login: Feb 28 | Submissions: 1 of 4 due
Course: SOC 150 — Last login: Mar 14 | Submissions: 2 of 3 due

**Google Sheets — 'R2T4 Tracking Spring 2026' (Row 28)**
Student: Park-Simmons, D. | WD Date: 3/14 | % completed: ???? | Calc by: T. Washington | Notes: 'Conflicting last attendance. Banner shows 3/14 official WD. Canvas shows last academic activity 3/14 for two courses but only 2/28 for MATH 210. Which date do we use? Using 3/14 per WD form. —TW'
[Cell highlighted yellow — no resolution noted]

**Slack — #finaid-team (Mar 20, 2026, 2:08 PM)**
@t.washington: Hey team — Park-Simmons R2T4 question. Kid withdrew 3/14 but his MATH 210 last activity was 2/28. Do we treat MATH as a class he never attended (reduce the payment period) or use the module-based definition since it's an online section?
@k.nakamura: Was it an online or hybrid section?
@t.washington: Online. East Campus course. Those old Eastview courses are weird — some still show as 'classroom' in Banner even though they moved online after the merge.
@k.nakamura: If it's truly online and modular, you'd use the last LMS activity date for that course. But if he submitted assignment 1 of 4, he DID begin attendance.
@t.washington: Right but that was week 2. He basically ghosted MATH after Feb 28.
@k.nakamura: Then his last date of attendance for R2T4 is still 3/14 — you use the latest activity across ALL courses in the period. MATH doesn't change the calc.
@t.washington: :eyes: oh wait. Shouldn't we check if the ENG 204 submissions on 3/14 were academically related? If they were just discussion posts...
[Thread ends — no response]

**Email — Subject: 'Fwd: Park-Simmons withdrawal circumstances' (Mar 16, 2026)**
From: academic.advising@brightpath.edu
To: finaid-withdrawals@brightpath.edu

'FYI — Daniel told his advisor he stopped attending MATH 210 in late February because the instructor wasn't posting materials. Department confirmed instructor had medical leave; no course activity Feb 25 - Mar 10. Replacement assigned Mar 11. May be relevant for your R2T4 since the student arguably couldn't attend.'
question: What is the correct last date of academically-related activity to use in Daniel Park-Simmons's R2T4 calculation, and why?

contributor.name: Jennifer Caldwell
contributor.title: Director of Financial Aid
contributor.domain_expertise: Federal financial aid (Title IV), SAP appeals, professional judgment decisions, institutional aid policy, Return to Title IV

choices: March 14 — use the official withdrawal date from the withdrawal form, as that is the institutional determination regardless of LMS activity patterns.
March 12 — use the PSYCH 301 last login as the last confirmed academic engagement, since discussion posts in ENG 204 on 3/14 may not qualify as academically-related activity.

March 14 — use the latest academically-related activity across all courses in the payment period (ENG 204 and SOC 150 submissions on 3/14), provided those submissions constitute academically-related activity.
February 28 — use the earliest 'last activity' date across courses (MATH 210) since he demonstrably disengaged from that course, reducing the payment period percentage.
